headline: Nine fired FBI employees sue. They call it payback.
summary: Nine FBI agents, analysts and specialists fired in February sued Thursday to get their jobs back. They worked the Mar-a-Lago classified documents case, assigned to it, not volunteers. The suit calls the firings political retribution and asks for reinstatement and back pay. Director Kash Patel told Congress those he fired weaponized the FBI.

cover_question.q: Why did they lose their jobs?

cover_answer: The boss says they picked sides. They say they did the job.
table_question: Should you be punished for a job you were told to do?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Nine people who worked at the FBI, the police for the whole country, lost their jobs in February. Their boss said they used the FBI against the president. They say they were doing the work they were given, like a kid told to clean the table who gets in trouble for cleaning it. Now they've asked a judge to decide, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: One cleaned table, one unfair telling-off, one judge to ask.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them and reads fairness through their own day, so the script turns the firing into the table they were told to clean and got in trouble for cleaning. One job, one boss, one judge to ask. Expect "did they do something bad?" They say no, the boss says yes, and that is what the judge is for.

8-12.script: In 2022 the FBI searched Trump's Mar-a-Lago home for classified papers. Nine agents and analysts assigned to that case were fired in February, after Kash Patel took over the FBI. He told Congress they weaponized it. They sued Thursday: a referee sent off for calling a foul on the owner's team, they say.
8-12.why: Search, new boss, firing, lawsuit. The referee is the mechanism.
8-12.why_long: This age is testing whether adults apply rules the same way to everyone, so the script hands over the chain in order: a search, a case, a new director, nine firings, a lawsuit. The referee is the mechanism: the agents say they were punished for the call, not for how they made it. Expect "will they get their jobs back?" Nobody knows yet.

13-17.script: Can you be fired for the case you were given? Nine FBI employees from the Mar-a-Lago case sued Thursday, calling their firings retribution. Patel says they weaponized the FBI; they say they were assigned, not volunteers. Second: as a podcaster Patel called the search unlawful. Can he judge its agents?
13-17.why: The president picks the director. The law sets how agents go.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can reason about what is not in front of them, so the script holds two true things: the president chooses the director, and the law still sets how an agent can be dismissed. Then it asks whether a director who called the search unlawful can judge the agents who ran it. Expect "who wins?" I don't know. It was filed Thursday.

5-7.q: Why did they lose their jobs?
5-7.a: Their boss said they used the FBI against the president. They say they only did the work they were given. A judge will sort it out.

8-12.q: What did they actually do wrong?
8-12.a: Patel says they weaponized the FBI. They say they did their job.

8-12.q: Can a boss fire you for who you investigated?
8-12.a: That's the question. The suit says they were owed a hearing.

13-17.a: Trump's case was dismissed in 2024 over the prosecutor's appointment.

13-17.q: Isn't a president allowed to pick his own FBI?
13-17.a: He picks the director. The suit says agents are owed a hearing.
